items.stem: Which of the following best describes "gradient"?
options: The point exactly halfway between two points, ((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2)
Lines that meet at a right angle; their gradients multiply to −1 (for non-vertical lines)
A line that rises from left to right, so y increases as x increases
The steepness of a line: change in y divided by the corresponding change in x
items.answer: The steepness of a line: change in y divided by the corresponding change in x
items.markingKey: D. "gradient" is the steepness of a line: change in y divided by the corresponding change in x.

items.stem: Briefly explain why the gradient of a vertical line is undefined.

items.markingKey: They divided the change in x by the change in y; gradient is rise over run, (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) = 3. (R1 A1)

items.stem: Sana writes: "A steeper line always has a larger gradient." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: Steepness depends on the size of the gradient; a line with gradient −5 is steeper than one with gradient 2.

items.stem: A student claims that y = 3x + 2 and y = 2x + 3 are parallel because they use the same numbers. Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Parallel lines need equal gradients; here the gradients are 3 and 2.
items.markingKey: Parallel lines need equal gradients; here the gradients are 3 and 2. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Ingrid says the distance from (0, 0) to (4, 6) is the same as the distance from (0, 0) to (6, 4). Explain why this is true.
